articleTitle: Problems associated with partial discharge detection calibration in large machines
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Discharges in Large Machines (Digest No. 1998/264)
abstract: The detection of partial discharges (PD) has become a standard technique towards the assessment of the integrity of the solid insulating systems of rotating machinery. The author discusses the calibration problem of PD detection instrumentation and whether a solution exists. The author then questions whether or not the problem is all that severe.

articleTitle: On-line detection of partial discharges in statorwindings of large turbine generators
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Discharges in Large Machines (Digest No. 1998/264)
abstract: Power utilities aim at the production of electrical energy at low cost and with a high availability. To achieve this for turbine generators, two aspects are of major importance: (i) minimal costs for maintenance; and (ii) reduction of in-service failures. This can only be realized when effective tools are available to assess the condition of a generator. In The Netherlands, common tools are: (i) online and offline diagnostics for stator windings; (ii) ultrasonic inspection of retaining rings; (iii) video endoscopes for visual inspections; and (iv) expert systems to calculate the risk-of-failure for stator and rotor windings. This paper describes one of these tools in detail, namely the online partial discharge monitoring of stator windings.

articleTitle: Identification of discharges in electrical machines-a manufacturing perspective
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Discharges in Large Machines (Digest No. 1998/264)
abstract: For many years, indications of the overall manufacturing quality of insulation systems for new stator windings have been provided by the results of loss tangent and breakdown tests carried out on randomly selected coils. Routine quality control tests have been used to confirm that a minimum level performance is maintained throughout the production sequence. The only standard measure of the condition of the main insulation in the completed winding has been loss tangent values. No acceptance limits are applied due to variable influences of stress grading and end winding geometry on the results obtained. After machines have been installed, an increased desire to ensure high service reliability has led to many users undertaking regular monitoring activities employing a wide variety of techniques. Procedures have been developed in response to situations which have been encountered. Significant experience has therefore been gained with particular approaches and this, in turn, has led to them being incorporated into specifications for future supplies. As a manufacturer, it has become necessary to evaluate a number of these methods to ensure conformance with purchaser's requirements. They can be categorised according to whether they are intended to identify discharge sites within the body of the insulation or on its surfaces.

articleTitle: Stator winding assessment using TVA probe
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Discharges in Large Machines (Digest No. 1998/264)
abstract: The TVA probe was first developed in North America for use in stator windings to establish deterioration of stator insulation due to void or slot discharges. The presence of voids particularly at the stack or corona discharge occurring in modern insulation systems is of major concern, given the requirements of end users for reliable systems. Since its introduction in the UK it has been developed into a tool for acceptance tests of 11 kV motor coils and generator bars.

articleTitle: Comparison of HV on-line condition monitoring
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Discharges in Large Machines (Digest No. 1998/264)
abstract: In-service condition monitoring of HV electrical plant (generators and HV motors) has expanded greatly in recent years. A number of different systems have been developed, some more successful than others. The relative effectiveness of the different monitoring systems is therefore of great importance in selecting the best method for installation for the type of plant to be monitored. This paper briefly reviews why in-service condition monitoring is needed and why it is cost effective. It reviews three of the available in-service monitoring systems and compares their relative sensitivities for the detection of partial discharge (PD) under simplified laboratory conditions. It considers the need for sensitivity checking or normalisation in result interpretation and comments upon the value of offline monitoring tests in support of in-service machine condition monitoring.

articleTitle: Very low frequency methods to detect discharge activity in large machines
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Discharges in Large Machines (Digest No. 1998/264)
abstract: This paper describes the outcome of a review of technical publications and other information concerning the development of very low frequency (VLF) test methods for HV insulation systems, and the use of those methods to investigate discharging in HV rotating electrical machines. The majority of papers concerned the development of VLF power supplies and their application to cable testing. ERA has several years of experience of applying VLF techniques to cables. There were very few papers concerning VLF tests on large machines. This paper is an attempt to draw together the development of this technology.
